expectations.text: The decline is specific - what cannot be done and why (the booking lead time) - not a generic apology.
expectations.evidence: The guidance says plainly that 'A decline needs three things. It comes early, it is specific, and it offers what does exist.' expectations.text: The decline is specific - what cannot be done and why (the booking lead time) - not a generic apology.
expectations.evidence: The transcript does not decline. It argues against declining ('"We technically can't." ... is not the same as "no interpreter exists"'), and the email says 'we're actively trying to book sign-language interpreters'. The only mention of a limit is 'Our local vendor can't supply them'. That names who can't help, but it never says the booking lead time is the reason. The email also opens with a general apology ('I'm sorry you had to ask for it with so little information on our site'). Conditional lines like 'If we can't give you what you need, we'll tell you plainly' don't say what can't be done
